BE IT ORDAINED BY THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE, WYOMING:
Section 1. That the owner(s) of the property described herein has (have) applied for a zoning
map amendment ("zone change") for said property in accordance with Section 2.2.1, Zoning Map
Amendment, of the Cheyenne Unified Development Code (*UDC").
Section 2. That on July 1, 2013, the City of Cheyenne Planning Commission conducted a public
hearing, reviewed the proposed zone change that is the subject of this ordinance, and recommended
approval of said zone change.
Section 3.That the Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne finds that the zone change that is
the subject of this ordinance meets the criteria specified in Section 2.2.1.d of the UDC.
Section 4. That, in accordance with Section 2.2.1, Zoning Map Amendment, Section 5.1.2,
Zoning Districts Established, and Section 5.1.3, Official Zoning Map, of the UDC, the aforementioned
application is hereby approved and the zoning classification of the real property described as Lots 1-3,
Block 1, Polk Addition, Cheyenne, Wyoming is hereby changed to LI Light Industrial.
Section5. That the City Engineer is hereby authorized and directed to alter and amend the
Official Zoning Map as described in Section 5.1.3 of the UDC to comply with the zone change as
described in Section 4 above when this ordinance takes effect in accordance with Section 7 below.
Section6.Sections, paragraphs, sentences, clauses and phrases of this ordinance are severable.
If any section, paragraph, sentence, clause, or phrase of this ordinance is declared unconstitutional, such
un constitutionality shall not affect any of the remaining sections, paragraphs, sentences, clauses, and
phrases.
Section7.That this ordinance shall be infullforce and effect upon its approval and publication
and upon the official filing of the affiliated Polk Addition final plat map with the County Clerk and Ex-
Officio Register of Deeds for Laramie County, Wyoming.

ZONE CHANGE DATA:
The applicant is requesting a Zone District Map Amendment (Zone Change)from AR
Agricultural Residential toLI Light Industrial for an 8.82 acre site in order to construct
commercial storage facilities upon the site.This zone change is being requested in conjunction
with and dependent upon the approval of a Street Vacation and Final Plat.
ZONE CHANGE ANALYSIS:
The subject property consists of three vacant parcels (replat in process) and includes vacated
portions of Cheyenne Street and Van Buren Avenue (street vacation in process).The 8.82 acre
side of the City on the northeast corner of Pershing Boulevard and Polk Avenue.To the west,
U.S.30 crosses Pershing Boulevard at a 45 degree angle which chops the area into a triangle and
creates a physical barrier between the subject property and the residential land uses to the north.
Dry Creek cuts along the northeast corner of the subject property and as a result portions of this
corner reside in a FEMA flood way or a100-year FEMA floodplain.
The subject property was annexed to the City in 2005 but is surrounded by County property to
the west, north and east.The subject propertyis currently zoned AR Agricultural Residential as
is the property to the north and east.To the south and across Pershing Boulevard is a MR-2
Medium-Density Residential-Developing zone district and to the west and across the street from
Polk Avenue reside AR, PUD Planned Unit Development and MU Mixed-use zoning districts.
Adjacent to the subject property to the north and east reside single-family homes on rural lots.To
the south ofthe subject property and across Pershing Boulevard reside single-family homes on
suburban lots.To the west and across from Polk Avenue resides a mix of residential, commercial
and industrial uses.The commercial and industrial uses include a storage park and a
manufacturer of asphalt and concrete sealer products.
The applicant is proposing to construct a storage park on the property.A storage park is defined
in the UDC as a Service Use where individual units are accessed independently from the exterior
ofa building through garage bay doors and are offered for rent or lease for the storage of
(LI) and Heavy Industrial (HI) zoning districts and permitted after conditional discretionary

requesting a zone change toLI.
The LI zone district is intended for offices, distribution and warehouses as well as manufacturing
and fabrication.Supporting retail uses and services are also appropriate as secondary uses. The
uses and building and site designs associated with uses in this district produce little or noimpacts
providing buffers to adjacent buildings and land uses to minimize the potential for incompatible
and negative impacts of uses in the district.
The City'sfuture land use plan, Shape Cheyenne, designates this specific area as Urban
Residential, the area to the west as Mixed-Use Commercial Emphasis and the area to the east as
Open Space &Parks.The purpose of the future land use plan is to provide a general framework
for neighborhoods and activity centers, not to predetermine specific land uses for individual
parcels, and is intended to provide some flexibility for the market to help determine which uses
are needed at a given time(Shape Cheyenne 2-8).
While LIis not an applicable zone district in the Urban Residential category, this property is
located within an area that could support an LI zone district based on the existing development
pattern and the natural and built features of the area. To the west reside commercial and
industrial land uses, which include a storage park, while a majority oftheland to the east resides
in a flood zone or flood plain and is not suitable or likely to be highly developed.Also, the
subject property is separated from residential neighborhoods by U.S. 30 and Pershing Boulevard
and its proposed use should produce little or no impact beyond its property line.Furthermore, the
applicant is proposing a use for the property that will serve the discretionary needs of a number
of residential neighborhoods.The location of the subject property to similar land uses to the west
and tobuilt and natural land features which provide buffers from residential areas may make it
appropriate for an LI zone district designation.

park.Also, the parcels are largely separated from residential uses by major roadways to the north
and south and Dry Creek to the east which provides buffers between the proposed use and the

and floodplain may be more appropriate for the proposed use as opposed to a residential use.
